level_title: Boss Trial: NullByte the Variable Golem

questions.title: Boss Phase 1/5: Charging Integer Mana
questions.prompt: NullByte raises a stone barrier! Assign the integer value 100 to the variable 'spell_power' to charge Alex's opening strike!
questions.code_snippet:
# Charge Alex's staff with 100 integer power
spell_power = ____
questions.explanation: Assigning a whole number without quotes (100) creates an integer (int) in Python and charges 100 spell damage!
questions.hint: Master PyWizard: Simply pick the raw number '100' without quotes or extra keywords!

questions.title: Boss Phase 2/5: The String Incantation
questions.prompt: NullByte's armor is weak to fire! Complete the code by assigning the string 'Ignis' to the variable 'spell_element'.
questions.code_snippet:
# Bind the fire element string to 'spell_element'
spell_element = ____
print("Casting " + spell_element)
questions.explanation: Text in Python is a string (str) and must be enclosed in quotes ('Ignis') so Python doesn't mistake it for an undefined variable!
questions.hint: Master PyWizard: Always wrap text in quotes—choose 'Ignis'!

questions.title: Boss Phase 3/5: Floating-Point Precision
questions.prompt: Alex scans NullByte's core frequency: 'core_freq = 3.75'. What data type does type(core_freq) return?
questions.explanation: Any number with a decimal point in Python is stored as a 'float' (floating-point number)!
questions.hint: Master PyWizard: Notice the decimal point in 3.75—decimal numbers in Python are always 'float'!

questions.title: Boss Phase 4/5: Variable Combo Multiplier
questions.prompt: NullByte is staggering! Multiply 'base_dmg' by 'combo' using the multiplication operator to calculate 'final_strike'!
questions.explanation: In Python, the asterisk (*) operator multiplies two numeric variables together (50 * 2 = 100)!
questions.hint: Master PyWizard: Python uses the asterisk '*' for multiplication, not 'x'!

questions.title: Final Phase 5/5: Ultimate Boolean Finisher!
questions.prompt: NullByte is at 100 HP! Arrange the code blocks in order to set 'core_exposed' to True, check the condition, and unleash the ultimate spell!
questions.explanation: Booleans must be capitalized (True). We declare the variable first, check it with 'if', and execute the indented action to shatter NullByte!
questions.hint: Master PyWizard: First assign 'core_exposed = True', then check 'if core_exposed:', and finally call the indented function!
